title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a hand calculation (numbered '5') of how the coordinate expression of a projective connection on a curve changes under a change of local coordinate. On the neighbouring pages Grothendieck works with a relative curve X/S, the line bundle ω, and the P^1-bundle P = P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)), the projectivised bundle of first-order principal parts (jets) of ω. There, sections disjoint from a given section σ correspond to connections on ω, and 'connexions projectives' correspond to a quadratic-differential-type datum c.

The local computation runs as follows.
- With s = s(t), he writes dt/ds = 1/s' and d(dt/ds) = -(s''/s'^2) dt.
- He derives the transformation law c_{D_s} = c_{D_t} + [-2(s''/s')' + (s''/s')^2] dt^2.
- He simplifies the bracket to (3s''^2 - 2s's''')/s'^2. This equals -2{s;t}, where {s;t} = s'''/s' - (3/2)(s''/s')^2 is the Schwarzian derivative.
- So c_{D_s} = c_{D_t} - 2{s;t} dt^2. This is the classical cocycle law for projective connections, up to the normalising factor -2 coming from his convention for c.

He then asks when c_{D_s} = c_{D_t}.
- Either s'' = 0, so s is affine in t.
- Or 3s''^2 = 2s's'''. This gives (log s'')' = (3/2)(log s')', hence s''^2/s'^3 = const, i.e. s'' = C s'^{3/2}.
- Integrating gives exactly the homographies s = (at+b)/(ct+d) = u_M(t), with M = (a b; c d).
- He verifies D_{u_M(t)} = D_t on generators of PGL_2: translations t+a, homotheties at, and inversion 1/t. For s = 1/t: s' = -1/t^2, s'' = 2/t^3, s''' = -6/t^4, so 3s''^2 - 2s's''' = 12/t^6 - 12/t^6 = 0.

Purpose: this identifies the standard projective structure on P^1 as PGL_2-invariant, i.e. projective connections as the structures whose transition maps are Möbius transformations. It feeds the next page, where horizontal sections of the projective connection on P lead to the Riccati equation dλ/dt + λ^2 = A. This is the classical Schwarzian/Riccati/second-order linear ODE correspondence.
errors: The intermediate logarithmic step is garbled. From 3s''^2 = 2s's''' one gets s'''/s'' = (3/2)(s''/s'), i.e. (log s'')' = (3/2)(log s')', i.e. 2 log s'' = 3 log s' + const. As transcribed, the coefficients 3/4 and 3/2 are inconsistent with this, although the final result s''^2/s'^3 = const is correct. This is either a slip on the page or a transcription misreading.
The case s''=0 (affine maps) is separated out, but it is already contained in the homography family (c=0). The constant C=0 case of s''=C s'^{3/2} likewise gives the affine maps. This is harmless.
The sign/normalisation convention for c (factor -2 times the Schwarzian) is nonstandard but internally consistent.

ideas.what: Transformation law of a projective connection under change of coordinate: c_s = c_t - 2{s;t} dt^2
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative cocycle for projective structures/projective connections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarz, Kummer; projective connections in Gunning's lectures 1966, Hawley–Schiffer)

ideas.what: Schwarzian vanishes iff s is a Möbius transformation; invariance of the standard projective structure under PGL_2, checked on generators
Projective connections viewed intrinsically on the P^1-bundle P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)) for a relative curve (context from neighbouring pages)
ideas.modern_name: Opers / indigenous bundles / sl_2-opers on relative curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (indigenous bundles), Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers), Mochizuki (indigenous bundles in p-adic Teichmüller theory)

missed.claim: The surrounding file combines Gauss–Manin connections, the Cartier operation, and an intrinsic jet-bundle treatment of projective connections on relative curves X/S. This suggests Grothendieck was handling projective connections algebraically over a base, a setting later central to Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory (indigenous bundles, p-curvature, dormant opers). This particular page is only the classical Schwarzian computation, so the connection rests on the dossier as a whole, not on this page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could document an early algebraic-geometric interest by Grothendieck in projective connections and opers over arbitrary bases, possibly alongside the Cartier operator. That would be of historical interest for the genealogy of indigenous bundles in char p.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correct, routine derivation of the Schwarzian transformation law and of its kernel (Möbius maps). Its only interest is the context: an intrinsic treatment of projective connections on relative curves on the neighbouring pages.
transcription_corrections: The log-derivative step should read (log s'')' = ((3/2) log s')' and 2 log s'' = 3 log s' + c^te. The transcribed 3/4 and 3/2 coefficients are inconsistent with the (correct) conclusion s''^2/s'^3 = c^te.
The first line labelled [-d(1/s)-] is a crossed-out false start, roughly 'dt/ds'.
'ou bien s''=0 i.e. s fonction affine de t' is written as a marginal note on the line 'Égalité c_{D_s}=c_{D_t} ssi ...'.
'3 types d'homographies' lists t↦t+a, t↦at, t↦1/t.
